title: A connected own domain opens the site on its own name through Tracy's proxy, is registered with Cloudflare for SaaS once proven, and is connected only after its hostname, its certificate and Tracy's own HTTPS probe say so
steps: S1: From the repo root at the commit under test, with TEST_DATABASE_URL removed from the environment: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/wordpress-access.test.mjs apps/tracy-host/test/site-publish.test.mjs packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/teardown-ingress.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/config.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/label.test.mjs (PHP must be installed: the two wordpress-access tests run the real plugin).

S2: With TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a PostgreSQL the run may create databases in: node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-timeout=120000 --test-force-exit apps/tracy-web/test/bar.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/site-address.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/site-publish.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/site-domain-provider.test.mjs

S3: In the output of S2 read the line of every test named under WITH_DATABASE in tests/regression/scripts/REG-PR-1048-own-domain-routing.mjs (the '#1037' tests of slice 1 and the SAAS*/ZONERENAME tests of slice 2).
S4: In the output of S1 read the line of every test named under WITHOUT_DATABASE in the same script.
expect: S1 and S2 each exit 0 with fail 0 and cancelled 0.

S4 FORGED and STRIPPED report ok: forged x-tracy-email / x-tracy-tier / x-tracy-role headers that reach the WordPress plugin unfiltered (the direct ingress route an own domain had before the fix) are given an administrator session; the same request through tracy-web reaches the site with no x-tracy-* header, nobody is signed in and no session cookie is issued.

S4 LEGACYRULE, ROUTEGEN, WEBSERVICE and ROUTEGENDOOR report ok: go-live.sh sends an own domain to tracy-web's local service (never 127.0.0.1:<site port>), replaces the site's own old direct rule, carries the run's route generation to the tunnel script, and adds nothing when the host does not know where tracy-web listens.

S4 INGRESSROUTE, GENERATION, RECORDUNREAD, RECORDWRITE, RECORDWHOLE, SERVICECHANGE, PORTALONE and TEARDOWN report ok: ingress_api.py owns a rule by its whole owner record (service, label, generation, previous), written ahead of the provider write and read back; a record that is missing, unreadable or unwritable never proves ownership or a route installed; an older generation or another site's label changes and removes nothing.

S3 WHOLEBODY, BACKOFFICE, LOCALHOSTS, ONEURL, SCRIPT, FORMATS, COMMENT, HEADERS, HTML, INTEGRITY and REFUSED report ok: on an own domain a URL is changed only as one complete value handed over by its format's parser whose origin is the site's; the site's name as another host's user part, a percent-encoded string and the right-hand side of a + stay byte for byte; a same-site asset loses its integrity hash while a CDN asset keeps it; a body that cannot be told whole is refused with 502 and x-tracy-own-domain-projection: refused.

S3 PROOF, NOTPUBLIC, TLS, NOTCONNECTED, LATEPROBE and GENRISES report ok: connected_at is written only after the route proof and a signed digest of the complete page read by an ordinary GET for this row and attempt; a replaced body, a kept header, an HTML prefix then a closed socket, 204/206, a stopped CMS, a private or mixed DNS answer and a late probe never connect.

S3 STANDING reports ok: a removal goes on only after the whole Tracy-address page was read through Tracy's proxy; a downgrade to http, a redirect loop, credentials in a redirect, 404/204/206 and a truncated body do not count.
S3 LEGACYPENDING and ROLLOUT report ok: a domain still on the old direct rule reads pending and is moved by the sweep itself with nobody pressing Publish.

S3 WHOLEAPP reports ok: a public hostname that is not Tracy's goes to the site router; connected is proxied, pending, released and never-held names are refused with Tracy's 404 page, and only an address inside the machine reaches Tracy's app.

S3 SAASCREATE, SAASSTATUS and SAASCONNECTED report ok: a custom hostname is created at the stand-in Cloudflare API only for a reservation whose _tracy TXT was proven, exactly once however often it is reconciled; pending validation reads HOSTNAME_PENDING, an active name with its certificate pending reads CERT_PENDING; the domain is not even probed until both are active, and is connected only when both are active and the HTTPS probe passed.

S3 SAASCONFLICT, SAASUNCONFIRMED and SAASLATE report ok: a hostname Cloudflare already holds (error 1406) is state conflict and never read, adopted or deleted; a create whose answer never arrived (timeout) is posting, recreated only when a lookup by name finds nothing, and never adopted or deleted when something is found; a create answered after the reservation went keeps its id and is deleted.

S3 SAASERRORS, SAASDELETE, SAASREADYDELETE and SAASTOKEN report ok: a refused create and an unreadable status are retried with a reason (REFUSED_HTTP_400, READ_HTTP_500, READ_TIMEOUT, READ_MALFORMED), and a failed read or an answer for another name makes the hostname not ready (HOSTNAME_UNREAD, HOSTNAME_CONFLICT) until a read succeeds; a hostname whose reservation was removed or whose site was deleted is deleted on the next pass, a 404 counts as deleted, and a failed DELETE or a 2xx with success false (DELETE_UNCONFIRMED) is kept with its id and retried; a late create answer on a deleting row is due for its delete at once; every validation record is kept whole, and an answer with more than can be shown whole is not read; the API token appears in no row, reading or log line.

S3 SAASCLAIM, SAASATTEMPT and SAASREADINESS report ok: a forced pass (Check DNS, the probe's read) takes no row another pass holds, so a create in the air is never looked up, re-sent or robbed of its id; a create's answer is written only on the row of that create attempt; a connected domain reads pending with CERT_FAILED or HOSTNAME_UNREAD when Cloudflare later reports its certificate failed or cannot be read, and connected again once a read succeeds; its connection then reads failed with the hostname's reason, never ok.

S3 SAASCLAIMGEN, SAASRECORDSID and SAASPROBEFRESH report ok: a pass whose claim ran out writes nothing on the row a later pass took and releases no claim but its own, and the hostname it was answered is kept in site_custom_hostname_orphan and deleted there by id, after which the name converges on one hostname of its own; a hostname whose validation records cannot be shown whole keeps its id and reads HOSTNAME_UNREAD until active, and a lookup holding an entry that is not a hostname is never read as empty; a probe whose hostname refresh did not read it (another pass holds the row, or the refresh failed) asks nothing and writes no reading.

S3 SAASEXACT reports ok: a read answered for another id than the row's is READ_MISMATCH (not ready, HOSTNAME_UNREAD) and never replaces the id on the row; a lookup by name holding an entry of another name is unreadable, so a row being deleted without an id is kept and nothing of the other name is deleted.

S3 SAASUNAVAILABLE, SAASCARD, SAASAUTO and ZONERENAME report ok: without Cloudflare for SaaS the custom-domain doors answer 503 OWN_DOMAIN_UNAVAILABLE and write nothing; the card names CNAME <domain> → connect.<zone> and the _tracy TXT, and lists any validation record Cloudflare returns; a name whose earlier hostname is still being deleted is refused 409 DOMAIN_RELEASING; a published site whose records are right is connected by the background sweeps with nobody pressing anything and without a routingTarget sent to the host; connect.<zone> and the fallback origin's name cannot become a Tracy address.

S4 SAASCONFIG, ZONELABELS and ZONELABEL report ok: CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID and CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_TOKEN are used only together — one alone leaves own domains unavailable and the server still starts — CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_API is refused in production, and no error carries the token; the CNAME-target and fallback-origin labels come from configuration (default connect, origin) and are refused as site labels.

selectors.removeDomainDoor: DELETE /api/sites/:key/address/domain ({name}; 502 DOMAIN_REMOVE_FAILED with step verify-address | restore-address | rollback-address)
selectors.customHostnameRows: site_custom_hostname (state creating | posting | created | conflict | deleting)

evidence: tasks/bang-chung/own-domain-routing.md — issue #1037: before the fix the host's ingress sent an own domain straight to the site's port, so client x-tracy-* headers reached Tracy Access unfiltered and were given an administrator session (test '#1037 reproduction' at plugin level, and on the stand's live WordPress through its direct site port).
fence: apps/tracy-web: bar/site-proxy.js + bar/own-domain.js + bar/own-domain-integrity.js (an own domain is proxied as its site with every x-tracy-* header and the tracy_sess cookie removed, format-aware origin projection, refusal of what cannot be told whole), sites/domain-probe.js (public-address pinning, route proof and signed whole-page proof), sites/address.js + sites/publish-store.js + sites/publish.js + cron.js (connected_at under the attempt's generation, addressStanding before removal, the rollout sweep), app.js (unknown public hostnames refused). apps/tracy-host + packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation: go-live.sh and scripts/provision/ingress_api.py (own domain → tracy-web's local service, owner record with service/generation/previous written ahead and read back). Slice 2: sites/site-domain-provider.js (custom hostnames created only for proven reservations, never adopted, deleted once the reservation is gone), address.js confirmOwnDomains (hostname and certificate gate before the probe and again in the writing transaction), cron.js sweepCustomHostnames + sweepOwnDomainStarts, sites/label.js zoneLabelRefusal.
